summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Ryuyu Saito studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.
Ryuzan Nishimoto was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Chishu Kitagawa and traditional teacher Chijo Kitagawa in 1916.

Ryōmin Akizuki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1944 to 1950. He taught Makio Takemura and held a post at Saitama Medical University around 1973.

Working in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics, Rüdiger Schmitt studied under Karl Hoffmann around 1963 to 1965. He held a post at Saarland University from around 1972 to 2004.
S. A. S. Sarma is an Indology scholar who held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, attested in 2004 and 2024.
S. Bhaskaran Nair was an Indologist who served as General Editor (attested 1944, 1992) and Deputy Director (attested 1974–1977, 1986) at the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute.

S. D. Laddu worked in Indology and linguistics. He was a colleague at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1968) and Editor of the Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 2003).
S. Ghosh worked in Tibetology and held posts as Librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology, both attested in 1982.

A scholar of Indology and philosophy, S. K. Ramanatha Sastri studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He worked as temporary staff at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and was Junior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras until 1938.

S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar studied at the University of Madras (graduating in 1897, M.A. circa 1897–1899). Working in Indology and history/archaeology, he lectured at Bengaluru City University (1899–1909) and held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at Madras (1914–1929).

S. Kuppuswami Sastri was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at St. Peter's College and the University of Madras. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College and Rajah's College, and Professor at Presidency College and Annamalai University.

S. M. Natesa Sastri was an Indologist who studied at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras. Around 1883, he worked at the Archaeological Survey of India as an assistant to Robert Sewell, and he taught Chembai Vaidyanatha Bhagavatar.

S. N. Balagangadhara studied at National College, Bangalore, and earned his doctorate under Etienne Vermeersch at Ghent University (1977–1991). Working in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, he directed Ghent University (circa 1991–2017) and co-chaired the American Academy of Religion (2004–2007).
S. N. Krishna is an Indology scholar who pursued doctoral studies at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under T. V. Vasudeva, attested in 2026.
S. N. Savadi was an Indologist who held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.
Shrinivas Narayan Tadpatrikar was an Indologist who held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1939 and as Supervisor of Collations in 1942.

Specializing in history, archaeology, and Indology, S. Rajavelu was an Assistant Superintendent Epigraphist at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 2011) and a Professor in Marine Archaeology at Tamil University (attested 2015).

S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who served at the University of Madras as Reader in Indian Philosophy (attested 1929) and Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 1942).

S. Sankaranarayanan worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Honorary Professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre from around 1986 to 1999 and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

S. Sankararama Sastri was an Indology scholar who served as a Pandit in the Publication Section of the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (attested 1943) and as a Pandit at the University of Kerala (attested 1944).
